summary: Tested new Live TV Favorites + Recently Watched endpoints and web UI. Backend: 5/5 pytest passed (auth guard on both endpoints, favorites add/upsert/delete, recent add/dedup/reorder/delete-one/clear-all, watched_at timestamp). Frontend /watch/live: verified initial empty rows hidden, star click adds favorite (API confirmed) and star fills gold, favorites row appears on reload and persists, clicking card body opens /watch/play/iptv-live-<id> and adds to recent, recent row shows on return, both rows are correctly hidden when search text is non-empty OR source chip != 'all', and reappear when the filter is cleared. No functional issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~2160 lines — still well past the 700-line threshold (called out in iter_9 too). The new live-favorites/recent block (~1895-1975) is well-scoped and could move into a small `backend/live_prefs.py` module along with movie/show favorites.

DELETE /api/me/live/recent (clear-all) is declared AFTER DELETE /api/me/live/recent/{channel_key} in server.py. FastAPI matches based on path template so this works correctly in practice, but declaring the more-specific fixed path (`/recent`) before the parameterised one is more idiomatic and future-proof against accidental catch-alls.
LiveChannelBody.number is typed as Optional[Any] which accepts both ints and strings (IPTV oddity). Fine, but consider a Union[int, str, None] for stricter validation and OpenAPI clarity.

add_live_favorite performs two separate update_one calls ($pull then $push) — not atomic. Under a fast double-click a race could theoretically leave a duplicate. Consider a single update with $pull+$push in one command or an aggregation-pipeline update.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (star toggle, persistence on reload, recent recording, filter-hides-rows all verified)
